_comment: api-growth-method.md §2's five evidence sources, collected at the end of
slice F. AUTHORED from measurements taken with the repo's own instruments;
every number below is reproducible by the command named beside it.
⚠ Slice F is the terminal slice: all three §4 conditions hold after it. §6
convergence and §4 are recorded here, and §3's derivation of a slice G is
name: rollback as a public promise

what_closed: `ambition_platformer2d::runtime` — all of it rollback. 10 uses across src/ and bin/: SnapshotState, Reader, put_f32, put_u32, RollbackRegistry, AmbitionRollbackApp, SyncTestSettings, start_sync_test_session.

`ambition_platformer2d::runtime::demo_fixture::ActorConstructionRegistry` — the last non-rollback use, and a separate leak wearing the loudest possible name. A module called `demo_fixture` in a shipped game's imports was the namespace mirror confessing. Re-published as `ambition_platformer2d::actor::ActorConstructionRegistry`: construction provenance is an ACTOR concept (ADR 0030), and that is where a consumer looks for it.

what_was_ADDED_to_the_allowed_set.⚠: This is a compatibility COMMITMENT, and the instrument cannot tell it apart from making the ratchet green. The review is the gate. It is justified only because slice F built the six properties ADR 0031 named and gave each one a test — not because the ratchet was at 1.

2b_fixture_leak_log.instrument: the diff, and `git show HEAD~1` for the before
2b_fixture_leak_log.what_the_22_lines_were: Ordering, and every line of it was a hazard the engine had already hit: activate before the session exists, because preparation and the session-world commit build the room and the body through `Commands` and a rollback cannot undo construction; then settle, because activation completing is not the same fact as the next tick being quiet. The first draft skipped both, started the session on update #1, and watched GGRS report a checksum mismatch on frames 2, 3 and 4 forever.
2b_fixture_leak_log.why_this_is_the_measurement_that_matters: The line count is a proxy. What the deletion proves is that the ordering is the ENGINE's to get right: a consumer who has never read that comment now gets the same startup. A third party could not have derived those two steps from anything published — they were learned by desyncing.
still_open: `SyncTestSettings` is no longer named by Outlander at all; `RollbackPlan` covers the two fields it actually set. The remaining fields (`players`) moved to composition, which is the point.

Prose in three fixture comments still SAYS `ambition_platformer2d::runtime::rollback` while describing history. Left deliberately: the SDK guards check CODE BLOCKS, and rewriting accurate history to satisfy a grep is how `api-prototype.md` §5 came to deny that a real module existed.

2c_blind_agent_run.latest: run 6 — zero engine files opened, 23 tool calls, first compile clean
2c_blind_agent_run.status_after_slice_F: NOT re-run. §4.2 was satisfied by run 6 and slice F adds public surface, so the honest position is that the condition holds for the surface run 6 saw and the rollback surface is UNTESTED by a blind author.
2c_blind_agent_run.⚠: This is recorded as a gap rather than assumed closed. A blind run over `ambition_platformer2d::rollback` is the first thing a slice G would do — see `after_the_terminal_condition`.

deleted_in_this_slice: `PlatformerApp::unstable_rollback_session` — the `#[doc(hidden)]` knob that existed so the engine's own rollback fixture could compose through the same builder as everything else. Replaced by `rollback(participants)`, which asks the question the hidden version could not.

`INTENTIONALLY_UNDOCUMENTED` in `test_sdk_api_reference_is_current.py` — its single entry was `unstable_rollback_session`. A waiver outliving its subject is precisely the stale entry the sibling ratchets forbid, so it went to an empty set rather than being left as a convenient home for the next awkward method.
2348 lines of `codecs.rs` (2688 → 340), which were never a design decision: the orphan rule forced them into one file.

became_deletable_and_was_NOT_deleted.verdict: NOT deletable, and the reason is a constraint rather than a preference. It implements `bevy_ggrs::Strategy`. Pulling `bevy_ggrs` into `ambition_platformer2d_core` would put the patched fork underneath every domain crate — and the floor's entire value is that a domain can reach it, which is true because it is small (zero workspace deps, `bevy_ecs` + `bevy_math` rather than the `bevy` umbrella).

KEPT, limits stated at the variant and in the test. It catches a broken COMPOSITION, not a consumer typo — the engine registers its own state, so a real rollback host is never empty. The consumer-facing half of the property is tested positively instead (`the_baseline_includes_state_the_engine_never_heard_of`).

written_and_deleted_before_shipping.what_it_did: Compared the declared participant count against `LocalSeatTopology` and refused when they differed.
written_and_deleted_before_shipping.why_it_looked_right: The shipped host reads the seat topology; a consumer declaring 'I am single-player' states something the engine cannot verify for it. Two sources that usually agree is the shape the observatory's own comments warn about.
written_and_deleted_before_shipping.why_it_went: It could never fire. A probe on a host composed through `PlatformerApp::rollback` found `LocalSeatTopology` ABSENT — the resource is inserted by the dev observatory's session path, not by the builder. So the check had no population on the public path.
written_and_deleted_before_shipping.⚠: Found by probing rather than by reading, and only because the variant shipped untested and that was noticed. An unreachable refusal reads as protection; this campaign's own header calls that an instrument that measures nothing and reports the success condition. The property it claimed to defend is enforced structurally instead — the count is not passable per session, so there is no second value to disagree with.
written_and_deleted_before_shipping.cost_of_the_lesson: One variant, ~30 lines, deleted the same day. The cost had it shipped is a future reader trusting a guard that cannot fire.

2e_capability_footprint.note: Unchanged, as expected: slice F moved code between crates and added a facade module, neither of which alters what depending on `ambition_platformer2d` links. The floor gained one inbound edge (`ambition_time` → `ambition_platformer2d_core`) and that crate was already in the closure.
2e_capability_footprint.⚠: This counter has not moved across the whole campaign, and it is the one §4 decomposition trigger that never fired. Recorded plainly rather than framed as stable: 19 crates a movement-only game never asked for is a real cost, it is measured, and no consumer has yet been unable to do something because of it.

4.2_blind_run_opens_no_engine_file.evidence: run 6: zero engine files, 23 tool calls, first compile clean

4.3_every_matrix_category_proven.evidence: 6 of 6 in consumer-matrix.json, each naming a test

§6_convergence.note: §6: every slice must strictly reduce at least one of five counters. Slice F reduced two and is the only slice that could reduce the first to zero.
§6_convergence.open_fixture_findings: blind run 6 named none; the rollback surface is unexamined by a blind author (recorded, not closed)
§6_convergence.undeleted_compensating_mechanisms: 6 → 4 (`unstable_rollback_session` and the SDK waiver that concealed it)

after_the_terminal_condition.⚠: §4 holding is not the same fact as the API being finished, and the campaign's own instruction is that a slice looking done means the next one needs deriving. What §4 says is that the three things the campaign chose to measure are satisfied — it does not say the measurements were sufficient.

known_gaps_that_a_slice_G_would_rank.cost: The newest public surface is the one most likely to send an author into `crates/`, and it is the only surface never put to the test §4.2 exists for. Cheapest of the three and the most likely to find something.
known_gaps_that_a_slice_G_would_rank.route: §3b: closeable + owned → the strongest slice-G candidate.

known_gaps_that_a_slice_G_would_rank.gap: 19 unwanted linked crates, unchanged across six slices
known_gaps_that_a_slice_G_would_rank.cost: The one §4 decomposition trigger that never fired. Still unfelt by any consumer, which is why it never won a ranking — and 'never felt' is itself six slices of evidence now, not an absence of data.
known_gaps_that_a_slice_G_would_rank.route: §3b: closeable + owned, and it is the last big structural question the campaign identified and did not answer.

known_gaps_that_a_slice_G_would_rank.gap: the consumer matrix is proven by consumers I wrote
known_gaps_that_a_slice_G_would_rank.cost: Every row is an in-tree fixture or an in-tree game. Outlander is external in dependency shape and internal in authorship. The matrix's own argument — an API proven against one consumer is shaped like that consumer — applies to authorship as well as count, and nothing in §4 measures it.
known_gaps_that_a_slice_G_would_rank.route: Not closeable by a slice. Recorded because it is the strongest reservation about the terminal condition and the campaign should not be read as having ruled it out.
